meta.title: Stock and warehouses · Clafina
meta.description: Know what you hold, where and what it is worth. Reorder levels, blind counts, transfers between places and valuation from one movement ledger.

hero.title: Know what you hold, where, and what it is worth.
hero.lede: Every movement goes into one ledger that only ever adds lines. Stock levels, counts, transfers and the stock value in your books all come from it.

jobs.title: Never run out
jobs.body: Set reorder levels for each item in each place. When stock reaches them, one button orders what needs it.

jobs.title: Count with confidence
jobs.body: Count on paper sheets or on a phone, blind if you like. Differences are posted as adjustments, and large ones wait for an approver.

jobs.title: Move stock under control
jobs.body: Transfers between places are followed while in transit and go through approval. Moves between inventory types carry your own reasons.

tour.title: See what needs ordering, worst first
tour.body: Each item in each place has a minimum, a safety level, a reorder point and a quantity to order. The list shows where each one stands.
points: Stock on its way between places is counted, but not sold
Sort your items into A, B and C classes
Order what needs it in one step

tour.title: Count, then approve
tour.body: A count sheet shows what has been counted and what differs. Approving it posts one adjustment for each line that does not agree.
points: Blind counts hide what is expected
Adjustments above a value go to an approver

tour.title: Count on the shop floor
tour.body: Counters walk the shelves with a phone, find an item by name or code and save each count as they go.

items.text: One movement ledger that only ever adds lines. See your stock as it stood on any past date.
Valuation by moving average or FIFO, with landed costs. The stock account in your books equals the value of your stock.
Name the vehicle or asset that carries a dispatch.
Inventory types such as raw materials, work in progress and finished goods. Hide the built-in ones and add your own.
Stock kept for each inventory type, with settings for which types a sale draws from.
Type transfers with your organisation's own reasons, which can be reversed.
Transfers between places, followed while in transit and sent through approvals.
Each person moves stock only in the places they are allowed to.
Reorder levels for each item in each place: minimum, safety level, reorder point and quantity. Order what needs it in one step.
Stock classes A, B and C, and cycle counts.
Count sheets with blind counts, and counting on a phone.
Blind counts set for each role.
On the phone, count by the carton or by the item, and see the bin each item sits in.
Products with variants, and service items next to goods.
Units of measure with conversions between them.
Batches and expiry dates.
Conversions for a single product, and document lines written in any of its units.
A price for each unit a product is sold in.
Adjustment requests that go to an approver above a value you set.
A mode where stock changes only through documents, never by hand.

connectsTitle: Connected to the rest of the business

connects.text: Orders, waybills and credit notes move stock in the place they come from.
Goods received add stock, and orders start from what needs ordering.
Stock value and every adjustment post to the ledger by themselves.
Production takes materials and puts finished goods into stock.
Tills sell from the same stock.
Your shop shows what is available to sell.

faq.q: Can I see what I held on a past date?
faq.a: Yes. Every movement is kept in one ledger that only ever adds lines, so you can see your stock as it stood on any day.

faq.q: Can counters count without seeing what is expected?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on blind counts and the expected number stays hidden until a count is saved.

faq.q: Can I stop people changing stock by hand?
faq.a: Yes. Adjustments above a value go to an approver, and you can choose a mode where stock changes only through documents.
